source_records.title: Time to get fit: open letter to Mark Zuckerberg and Meta board

facts.status: Existing long-term shareholder; supportive of founder/product leadership, critical of excess spending.
facts.plan: Reduce headcount expense at least 20%; cap annual capex at $25B, $5B below $30B; limit metaverse spending to $5B/year.
facts.FCF_target: Approximately $40B in 2023 versus roughly $20B, via people/capex/metaverse expense discipline.
facts.valuation: P/E declined from 23x to 12x, less than half the average P/E of big-tech peers. The letter does not specify forward earnings or a decade-average 23x.
facts.distinction: Supports high-return AI investment; demands measured returns and bounded funding for uncertain, long-dated projects.
facts.attribution: Public request, not proof Meta management followed the letter or trades occurred on publication date.

source_records.title: SEC: Frequently Asked Questions About Form 13F
evidence_notes: Current page update; last-reviewed 2026-09-28. Earlier original-page date 2023-05-24.

facts.coverage: Quarter-end covered long securities under investment discretion; generally U.S.-exchange stocks/ADRs and certain options, warrants and convertibles.
facts.lag: Quarterly filing due within 45 days, subject to applicable calendar rules.
facts.excluded: Short positions and written options; foreign-only listed stocks, private investments, cash and many other assets. Long/short positions must not be netted.
facts.omissions: Small holdings may be omitted only if both under 10,000 shares and under $200,000; confidential treatment can delay disclosure.
facts.aggregation: A manager filing can aggregate several accounts or other included managers. Sole discretion does not identify the individual who selected a position.
